title: Arkansas's 3rd Congressional District general election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Arkansas's 3rd Congressional District will determine who represents the northwest Arkansas region, including Benton, Carroll, Crawford, Madison, and Washington counties and part of Sebastian County. Incumbent Republican Steve Womack, first elected in 2010, is seeking reelection after winning an uncontested Republican primary on March 3, 2026. He faces Democrat Robb Ryerse, a pastor and nonprofit leader who switched parties after challenging Womack in the 2018 Republican primary, and independent Christopher Hocevar, a University of Arkansas doctoral candidate and teacher. The district is rated 'Solidly Republican' by the Cook Political Report, making Womack the strong favorite in the general election.

candidates.name: Steve Womack
candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 3rd Congressional District since 2011. A senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, Womack chairs the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Subcommittee and formerly served as Chairman of the House Budget Committee. Prior to Congress, he served as Mayor of Rogers, Arkansas for 12 years and retired from the Arkansas Army National Guard as a Colonel after more than 30 years of military service.

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Steve Womack consistently defends Second Amendment rights and opposes broad federal gun-control legislation. He supported overturning the ATF's stabilizing brace rule (HJ Res. 44) in 2023 and voted against the Senate gun-control bill in 2022.

sources.title: Womack Votes to Overturn ATF Stabilizing Brace Rule
Womack Statement on Senate Gun-Control Legislation

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Supports election integrity measures that require citizenship verification and photo ID for federal elections, asserting that only U.S. citizens should vote. He voted in favor of the SAVE America Act (S.1383) to implement those protections, including removing noncitizens from voter rolls.

sources.title: Womack Votes for SAVE America Act to Safeguard Federal Elections
Vote Record | U.S. Congressman Steve Womack - House.gov

Election Policy.stance: Steve Womack voted in support of S.1383, the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (SAVE Act). The bill would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections, require photo ID to vote, and require states to remove noncitizens from voter rolls.

Education.stance: Supports limiting federal involvement in K-12 education and giving states and local communities more decision-making authority over standards and accountability. Believes in expanding educational options and pursuing higher-education reforms to improve access and affordability.

sources.title: Education | U.S. Congressman Steve Womack - House.gov

Economy.stance: Steve Womack supports pro-growth, low-tax economic policies, including lowering taxes, reducing regulatory burdens, and supporting American energy development to strengthen and grow the U.S. economy.

Healthcare.stance: Supports the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act (H.R. 6703), which aims to reduce health care premiums and costs through transparency and expanded coverage options; he stated he would have voted in support of the act in Congress to deliver more affordable health care to Arkansans in the 3rd District.

sources.title: Womack Supports Bill to Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans

Local Issues.stance: Supports targeted local infrastructure funding to address transportation, water system upgrades, and public safety needs in Arkansas's Third District. This includes advocacy for and highlighting Community Project Funding for local projects such as highway improvements and water infrastructure upgrades.

Foreign Policy.stance: Steve Womack supports a strong, globally engaged U.S. foreign policy that prioritizes national security, defense readiness, and enduring alliances. He backs targeted foreign aid—such as Israel security assistance—and robust defense spending to promote security and economic growth for the United States.

candidates.name: Robb Ryerse
candidates.summary: Pastor and nonprofit leader running for Congress in Arkansas's 3rd District. A former Republican who switched to the Democratic Party, he previously challenged incumbent Steve Womack in the 2018 Republican primary. He co-founded Vortex PAC with Dr. Chris Jones and worked with Vote Common Good to combat extremism. Ryerse has lived in Springdale for 20 years with his wife Vanessa and raised four children, and pastors Vintage Fellowship, a faith community that meets monthly.

candidates.name: Christopher Hocevar
candidates.summary: Christopher Hocevar is an independent candidate for Arkansas's 3rd Congressional District in the 2026 general election. A doctoral candidate in Materials Science at the University of Arkansas, he holds an engineering degree from the University of Oklahoma and works as a teaching and research assistant. His campaign focuses on housing affordability, healthcare access, teacher pay, student loan reform, raising the minimum wage, and reducing corporate influence in politics. Originally from Ponca City, Oklahoma, Hocevar was inspired to run after conversations with local small business owners about permitting and regulatory burdens.

Immigration.stance: Hocevar supports funding the Department of Homeland Security, including ICE, but insists on strong oversight and accountability. He argues that with the federal deficit, every dollar spent should be justified and transparent.

Healthcare.stance: Hocevar supports defending Medicaid and promoting bills that ease enrollment in affordable healthcare programs. He notes that nearly 9% of 3rd District residents are uninsured and that the number of uninsured children in Arkansas has risen drastically. He advocates for ensuring federal healthcare funding is used to benefit local communities and not wasted.

Economy.stance: Hocevar advocates for fiscally responsible federal budgeting with rigorous oversight to ensure spending is efficient and necessary, including accountability for DHS funding. He also supports raising the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour for full-time workers and adjusting tipped workers' wages accordingly, arguing the current $7.25 an hour does not provide a livable income.

Local Issues.stance: Hocevar focuses on housing affordability and availability in Northwest Arkansas, advocating for reducing private investment firms' role in the housing market and shifting more control to cities and states. He also emphasizes reducing hunger and expanding healthcare access. His platform includes supporting agriculture infrastructure to keep economic benefits local.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of the AR-03 2026 House race with strong documentation across all four candidates. The incumbent Steve Womack's positions are backed by official House.gov sources, campaign materials, and legislative records (OpenSecrets, Congress.gov). Challenger Robb Ryerse's stances are documented via his campaign website and social media. Independent Christopher Hocevar's platform is sourced from his campaign site and news coverage. Libertarian Bobby Wilson's minimal issue coverage reflects genuine absence of public positions rather than research failure. Language is consistently neutral across all candidates—no loaded adjectives, no asymmetric framing between opposing candidates' similar positions (e.g., both Womack and Ryerse on economy are described neutrally). Career histories are internally consistent with cited sources. The profile appropriately flags low-confidence stances where research found no public position, which is acceptable for minor-party and first-time candidates. Minor gaps in sourcing for some career history fields (e.g., Womack's military service lacks a direct URL) are not material given the corroboration from multiple biographical sources.

flags.concern: The FEC link for Steve Womack (H6AR03128) is noted in the profile as pointing to Ryerse; this is a minor administrative discrepancy.
flags.suggestion: Update the link to the correct FEC ID for Steve Womack (H0AR03128) to ensure users reach the intended data.

flags.concern: The profile notes the candidate signed a pledge to 'abolish ICE'. While this is sourced, the term 'abolish ICE' is a highly charged political slogan that can be interpreted differently by various audiences.
flags.suggestion: Consider adding a brief, neutral clarification of what the candidate means by this (e.g., 'advocating for a restructuring of immigration enforcement agencies') if the candidate has provided such context in their materials.

flags.concern: The summary field for Bobby Wilson is empty.
flags.suggestion: Even for minor-party candidates, a brief sentence summarizing their platform or background (e.g., 'Libertarian activist from Bentonville') would improve completeness.

reviews.summary: The profile is exceptionally well-researched, providing a balanced and neutral overview of all candidates in the race. It effectively handles the challenge of varying levels of public information by clearly documenting where positions were not found, and it maintains a consistent, objective tone across all candidate summaries. The sourcing is robust, particularly for the incumbent, and the formatting is clean and professional.

Strong sourcing across candidate platforms and voting records, with high-confidence stances tied directly to official House.gov documents, campaign websites, and credible local news. Career histories and summaries are internally consistent with cited sources (Ballotpedia, FEC, womack.house.gov, robbforcongress.com). forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, which suppresses confidence. However, the structural indicators are unambiguous: incumbent Steve Womack (R) has represented this district since 2011, holds a senior position chairing the House Appropriations Transportation-HUD subcommittee, and has a commanding financial advantage ($2.3M cash on hand vs. challengers with minimal or no reported fundraising). The Cook Political Report rates AR-03 as 'Solidly Republican.' The Democratic challenger (Robb Ryerse, a former Republican who lost to Womack in the 2018 GOP primary), the independent challenger (Christopher Hocevar, a first-time candidate and doctoral student), and the Libertarian candidate (Bobby Wilson, who received 4.43% in 2024) all lack the institutional, financial, or electoral track record to threaten the incumbent in a strongly Republican district. Womack's uncontested Republican primary further signals a consolidated base. The 34-point margin estimate reflects the district's heavily Republican lean and Womack's consistent past performance (62.8% in 2024). Confidence is medium rather than high solely due to the absence of any public polling to validate these structural signals.
